questions.question:
Four different segments of a DNA molecule are represented below.

   Segment 1: T-A-G-G-C / A-T-C-C-G
   Segment 2: C-G-T-G-A / G-C-A-C-T
   Segment 3: G-A-T-T-A / C-T-A-A-T
   Segment 4: C-A-A-T-G / C-T-T-A-C

Find the segment which is an ERROR paired.
questions.answer_guide: Segment 4 has an error: the first pair is C paired with C, but in DNA C pairs with G (A pairs with T).

questions.answer_guide:

      K. Sensory neuron
      L. Relay (intermediate / connector) neuron
      M. Motor neuron

      b) Chemicals (neurotransmitters) that diffuse across the gap
      c) Draw the arrow along neuron K pointing from the sharp nail (finger) towards the spinal cord
      d) The sharp nail (a pricking / pain stimulus)
      e) Any two: heartbeat, breathing, peristalsis (movement of food in the gut), blinking, sneezing, knee jerk, pupil reflex

B.
   I.
      A. Cornea
      D. Retina
      E. Optic nerve
   II. (the figure is small, so check against the original)
      C. (iris) The circular muscles contract and the radial muscles relax, so the iris gets bigger and the opening gets smaller, which reduces the light entering the eye
      B. (pupil) The pupil becomes smaller (constricts)
   III. A - 2 (cornea refracts light rays); C - 1 (iris controls the amount of light); D - 3 (retina contains light receptors); E - 4 (optic nerve carries impulses to the brain); F - 5 (the paper lists F for 'focuses light', but the lens is the part that focuses light; check the lettering against the original)

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (80 MARKS) - QUESTION THREE: ENDOCRINE SYSTEM AND HOMEOSTASIS (11 MARKS)
questions.question:
A. The given table below is the endocrine system.
   i. Complete the following table by filling in the blank spaces (7 marks)
      Name of gland     | Hormone produced | One important function
      Pancreas (islets) | ................ | Lowers blood glucose concentration in the body
      Thyroid           | ................ | ................
      ................  | Adrenaline       | ................
      Testis            | ................ | Regulates the development of male secondary sexual characteristics
      ................  | Estrogen         | Regulates the development of female secondary characteristics

   ii. Briefly explain why the pituitary gland is called the master gland (2 marks)

   iii. Define the term homeostasis and give one example (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A.
   i.
      Pancreas (islets): Insulin
      Thyroid: Thyroxine; function: controls the metabolic rate (and growth and development)
      Adrenal gland: Adrenaline; function: prepares the body for fight or flight (increases heart rate, breathing rate and raises blood glucose)
      Testis: Testosterone
      Ovary: Estrogen
   ii. The pituitary gland is called the master gland because it produces hormones that control the activities of other endocrine glands (such as the thyroid, adrenals and gonads).
   iii. Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant internal environment of the body. Example: regulation of blood glucose level (by insulin and glucagon), body temperature or water balance.

questions.question:
A. The diagram shows a mosquito feeding on human blood.
   Mosquitoes can carry transmissible diseases such as malaria.

   i) Define the term disease. (1 mark)

   ii) The human body has several defenses against diseases. State the name of two chemical barriers in the body.
      1. ........................ (1 mark)
      2. ........................ (1 mark)

   iii) Typhoid is one of the bacterial diseases.
      a) Name the pathogen that causes this disease (1 mark)
      b) Explain how this disease can be treated (cured). (1 mark)

   iv) Treponema pallidum is a pathogenic bacterium
      a) Name the disease that this pathogen causes (1 mark)
      b) State the way of transmission of the disease in your answer (i) (1 mark)

   v) Mosquito is an insect vector that transmits malaria. Give two other insect vectors
      1. ........................ (1 mark)
      2. ........................ (1 mark)

   vi) Classify the diseases in the box by their transmission modes, by using the table below. (8 marks)
      [ Common cold, Ringworms, Tuberculosis, Rabies, Cholera, Gonorrhea, Cystic fibrosis, Syphilis. ]
      Air-borne disease | Contagious Disease | Pet-borne disease | Water/food-borne diseases | STDs | Inheritance

questions.answer_guide:
A.
   i) A disease is a disorder (a condition that stops part or all of the body from working normally), usually caused by a pathogen or by a faulty gene or lifestyle.
   ii) Any two chemical barriers:
      1. Hydrochloric acid in the stomach
      2. Lysozyme in tears and saliva (also: acid on the skin, earwax, mucus)
   iii)
      a) Salmonella typhi (a bacterium)
      b) With antibiotics
   iv)
      a) Syphilis
      b) Sexual contact (it is a sexually transmitted disease)
   v) Any two other insect vectors:
      1. Tsetse fly
      2. Housefly (also: flea, louse)
   vi) See the matching pairs: Air-borne: common cold, tuberculosis; Contagious: ringworms; Pet-borne: rabies; Water/food-borne: cholera; STDs: gonorrhea, syphilis; Inheritance: cystic fibrosis.

diagram.caption: Steps in insulin production: a gene (Q) is cut from a human cell; a bacterium's plasmid is cut open and the gene is inserted to make R; R is put into bacteria (transgenic bacteria), which are grown in culture; the product is collected in a bottle (S).

questions.answer_guide:
A.
   Q. The human insulin gene (the piece of DNA cut out of the human cell)
   R. Recombinant plasmid (a plasmid that now carries the human insulin gene)
   S. Insulin (the product, in a bottle)

B. Bottle S contains human insulin, which is used to treat diabetes (to lower blood glucose in people whose bodies cannot make enough insulin).

C. Milk is pasteurized (heated) to kill harmful bacteria and other microbes, so that the useful bacteria added (lactic acid bacteria) can grow and make yogurt or cheese safely.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (80 MARKS) - QUESTION SIX: ADVANCED GENETICS (16 MARKS)
questions.question:
A. Organisms pass on their genetic information in their gametes
   A homozygous rabbit for black fur was crossed with homozygous a rabbit for brown fur. All of their offsprings had black fur.
   Parents: homozygous black fur male (BB) × homozygous brown fur female (bb)

questions.answer_guide:
A.
   i)
      Homozygous: having two identical alleles for a gene (e.g. BB or bb)
      Heterozygous: having two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Bb)
   ii)
      Dominant allele: B (black fur)
      Reason: all the F1 offspring from the cross of black and brown parents had black fur, so the black allele masks the brown allele
   iii) Cross: bb × Bb
      Gametes: (1) b  (2) b  +  (3) B  (4) b
      Offspring genotypes: 1 Bb, 2 bb, 3 Bb, 4 bb
      Offspring phenotypes: 1 black, 2 brown, 3 black, 4 brown
      Ratio: 2 brown : 2 black (1 : 1)

B.
   i. A nucleotide (of DNA / RNA)
   ii.
      X. Phosphate group
      Y. Sugar (five-carbon sugar, deoxyribose in DNA)
      Z. Nitrogenous base
   iii. Uracil pairs with adenine (A) (in RNA)
